presentation.label: Temp Save
presentation.summary: FUNC + YES keeps a temporary copy of the active pattern and its Part; FUNC + NO puts both back, as Temp Save and Reload do on the Digitakt and Digitone.
presentation.overview: Got a groove you like? Press FUNC + YES on the pattern screen to keep a temporary copy of the pattern and its whole Part, scenes included. Experiment freely, then press FUNC + NO to bring both back at once, even while the sequencer plays. The copy is separate from the saved Part and the copy/paste clipboard, so RELOAD PART and pattern paste work as before.
highlights: One gesture keeps the pattern (trigs, locks, length, scale) and the whole active Part: machines, every page, both effects and the scenes.
FUNC + NO restores both at once, also while playing; the crossfader, the selected scenes and the mutes stay where your hands left them.
Separate from the saved Part and the clipboard: RELOAD PART still goes back to your last Part save, and copied patterns or tracks stay on the clipboard.
On another pattern, bank or project FUNC + NO shows NO TEMP SAVE and changes nothing.
usage: On the pattern screen (no menu or list open), press FUNC + YES: TEMP SAVED.
Change the pattern and the Part as you like: trigs, knobs, scenes, machines.
Press FUNC + NO: RELOADED. The pattern and its Part are back as they were at FUNC + YES.

limitations: OS 1.40C. Tested by hand on one MKII over USB; the MKI and the card build were not run on a unit.
One temporary copy, of one pattern and its Part, kept in the module's memory: gone after a power-off and never written to the card. Save the Part and the project to keep your work.

FUNC + YES and FUNC + NO on the pattern screen no longer repeat ARM ALL and DISARM ALL; YES and NO alone still do. In menus, windows and sample lists both gestures stay stock (FUNC + YES still previews samples).
The reload replaces the pattern and the Part as a whole, including edits made since FUNC + YES on any track; the Part then counts as edited, as after a paste.
Another project, or this one saved under another name, makes the copy unusable (NO TEMP SAVE).
Uses 816 bytes of code and a 42,892-byte buffer; over USB from the module pool all modules share.

storage.label: Storage
storage.display: 824 B of code plus a 42,892 B copy buffer; no DSP code, no saved data
storage.conditions: The USB package of commit 001fc493: 824 bytes of code and data, 42,892 bytes of bss. On the card build the unit sits in the platform's DRAM reserve.

processing.label: CPU / DSP load
processing.display: None while idle; ~16k instructions a save, ~640k a reload (emulator)
processing.conditions: ot_emu, executed instructions from the hook's entry, interrupts included: a save to its toast 16,287 (up to 39,151 under a MIDI flood), a reload to the end of its screen refresh 637,251 stopped and 640,923 playing; no DSP work. Under a MIDI flood the longest frame interrupt rose 0.3 us and idle fell 0.2 points against stock. Time on the unit not measured.

impact.conditions: One reload while the sequencer plays; nothing runs between presses.

cpu.rationale: No idle cost. A save copies about 43 KB (16,287 executed instructions under ot_emu); a reload runs stock's pattern writer, Part Reload and screen refresh (about 640,000 instructions, most of them stock's). Time on the unit is not measured.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code. The restored Part reaches the DSP through stock's own Part apply, as RELOAD PART does.

memory.rationale: A 42,892-byte buffer for one pattern and one Part, plus 824 bytes of code: on USB about a sixth of the 256 KB module pool all modules share; no saved data.

tests.summary: On one MKII over USB (28 Oct 2026), by hand on the flashed base beside 13 kept modules: save, reload of trigs, parameters, a machine change and a Part change, reload while playing, NO TEMP SAVE on another pattern, stock behaviour in menus, sample lists, YES/NO alone and FUNC + CUE, and quick double presses (fixed in this source after the first run). Under ot_emu (verify.py, 37 checks MKII, 34 MKI): the pattern and Part restored byte for byte in RAM and their battery copies, Part switch, bank without saved Parts, MIDI mode, windows, key order, power cycle; beside Apply Scene, Preview Vol and Direct Jump.

conditions.parameterExtremes: The dearest event is a reload while playing: 640,923 executed instructions from the FUNC + NO hook to the end of the screen refresh (verify.py); under a 1,000 message/s MIDI flood 16 reloads took 605,222 to 635,604. A save took 16,287 (39,151 at most under the flood).
conditions.parameterModulation: Not applicable: one save or reload per press, outside the audio frame. The restored values are pattern and Part bytes that the sequencer, scenes and LFOs read as usual.
conditions.modeSwitching: Save, reload, a repeated quick press, a reload after a machine change, after a Part change and on a bank whose Parts were never saved, stopped and playing, MIDI mode.
conditions.maxLoad: Executed ColdFire instructions under ot_emu, interrupts included; one instance. Budget: 100 ms of ColdFire time at 266 MHz, a key-press responsiveness target, not a measured limit. No static bound: the reload's cost is stock's pattern writer 0x4002b9b0, Part Reload 0x4004aab4 and screen refresh, which nothing in this repository bounds.
conditions.inputConditions: Independent of audio and MIDI; runs in the UI task once per press. Executed instructions, not cycles: cache and wait states are not modelled, and time on the unit is not measured.

regions.name: ColdFire code and state (one linked unit)
The temporary copy: one pattern (36,568 bytes) and one Part (6,322 bytes)

memory.conditions: The unit as the USB package carries it (824 bytes of code and data, 42,892 bytes of bss). No DSP memory, no saved data.

hardware.summary: On the contributor's Octatrack MKII (OS 1.40C), flashed personal base beside 13 kept modules, the USB package of this source (SHA-256 above) ran as a timed trial installed with the device tool. By hand: FUNC + YES and FUNC + NO saved and restored trigs, parameters on several tracks, a machine change and a pattern moved to another Part; reloads while playing worked; another pattern showed NO TEMP SAVE; quick double presses saved and reloaded again; in MIXER, PROJECT, trig edit, PATTERN SETTINGS and SRC SETUP both gestures stayed stock, the sample preview played, YES and NO alone and FUNC + CUE behaved as stock, and Apply Scene's SCENE + YES still worked. The first package of this run (an earlier source) failed the quick double press, which this source fixes.
limitations: One unit, tested by the contributor, not an independent reviewer; the MKI was not tested.
USB only: the card build was not flashed.
Nothing timed; a reload while playing was judged by ear only.
Timed trials only: the site's review, Keep and Undo flow and a power cycle with the module kept were not used.
MIDI mode, other banks and a project save after a reload ran under the emulator only.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: On the pattern screen, with no menu open, place a few trigs and press FUNC + YES: TEMP SAVED.
Change the pattern and the Part: clear some trigs, turn knobs on two pages, try another machine.
Press FUNC + NO: RELOADED. The trigs, knobs and machine are back as they were at step 1.
To keep the result, save the Part (FUNC + PART, SAVE) and the project.
